events.title: St Jerome dies in Bethlehem
events.description: The scholar Jerome died in Bethlehem, where he had translated most of the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek. His Vulgate became the standard Bible of the Western Church for over a thousand years.
events.html: The scholar Jerome died in Bethlehem, where he had translated most of the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek. His Vulgate became the standard Bible of the Western Church for over a thousand years.

events.title: Theodoric the Great defeats Odoacer at the Battle of Verona
events.description: Theodoric the Great, leading his Ostrogoths in person, won a decisive victory at Verona over Odoacer, king of Italy, who fled to Ravenna. Theodoric was then free to take Pavia and Milan, and by 493 he ruled Italy.

events.title: Türgesh tribesmen capture the baggage train of an Umayyad army
events.description: Retreating across the Oxus from Khuttal, the Umayyad army of Asad ibn Abdallah al-Qasri lost its baggage train, sent ahead, to the pursuing Türgesh. The failed campaign ended Arab control of the upper Oxus valley and opened Khurasan to the Türgesh.

events.title: Cardinal bishops alone elect Pope Alexander II
events.description: Under Nicholas II's bull In Nomine Domini, the cardinal bishops were the sole electors of a pope for the first time, choosing Anselm of Baggio, Bishop of Lucca. Opposition to the election forced his coronation into San Pietro in Vincoli, not St. Peter's.

events.title: A great earthquake strikes the Caucasus near Ganja
events.description: One of the worst earthquakes in history struck around Ganja, in lands of the Seljuk Empire and the Kingdom of Georgia. Its disputed death toll of 230,000 to 300,000 makes it one of the deadliest earthquakes ever recorded.

events.title: An Anglo-Breton army defeats a larger Franco-Breton force at Morlaix
events.description: Near Lanmeur in Brittany, an Anglo-Breton army defeated a far larger Franco-Breton force in the first land battle of the Hundred Years' War. England had sided with John of Montfort in the Breton Civil War, France with Charles of Blois.

events.title: Parliament accepts Richard II's deposition and Henry IV's claim
events.description: Richard II's abdication was read to an assembly at Westminster, which then acclaimed Henry Bolingbroke as Henry IV. The Lancastrian usurpation sowed the seeds of the Wars of the Roses.
events.html: Richard II's abdication was read to an assembly at Westminster, which then acclaimed Henry Bolingbroke as Henry IV. The Lancastrian usurpation sowed the seeds of the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: The Lebanese Council opens to reform the Maronite Church
events.description: Maronite and Latin clergy under Yusuf ibn Siman as-Simani met at the monastery of Our Lady of Luwayza near Zouk Mosbeh to address the church's dependency on the aristocracy and the patriarchs' rights. Its decrees took several decades to carry out.

events.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute premieres in Vienna
events.description: Die Zauberflöte opened at the Theater auf der Wieden with Mozart conducting. It was a popular success, and he died nine weeks later at the age of 35.

events.title: Chamberlain returns from Munich promising 'peace for our time'
events.description: Neville Chamberlain landed at Heston waving the declaration signed with Hitler and later spoke of 'peace for our time'. Within six months Germany had seized the rest of Czechoslovakia.

events.title: James Dean dies in a car crash aged 24
events.description: Actor James Dean was killed when his Porsche collided with another car in California. Two of his three starring films were released after his death, making him a lasting icon of youth.
